handling_contacts: external bottom in shaped pusher cup
interface_contract.receiver_support: Two split lower seats close around the lifted exterior; the pusher can then retract through their central opening

handoff_sequence: Confirm receiver aligned and fully open; donor tube present; frame/dock secured
Close and verify lid before real transfer; lid mechanism is not modeled in H02
Approach external bottom slowly with shaped pusher; confirm contact within qualified force limit
Lift tube under controlled support to receiver capture height
Close split receiver seats and body guides; independently verify capture and tube identity
Retract pusher only after capture confirmation; stop on missing or contradictory feedback
Move receiver away only with closed receiver and fully retracted pusher
limitations: Article-specific tube dimensions and all clearances are illustrative; no fabrication release
Open windows show geometric access only, not proven visibility of real transparent liquid or a wall droplet
The blue fluid patch is an illustration; no sample volume or optical detection is validated
Lower seat edges and pusher cups require real contact, force, deformation and repeatability tests
Receiver jaws and actuator housings are mechanism envelopes; compliance, drives and grip sensors are not selected; handling remains upright with qualified accelerations still to be determined
TubeLift is an imposed visualization coordinate; support/contact checks do not simulate gravity, friction or flexible plastic
Lids and lid actuators are omitted; actual parked/closed cap envelopes and spill control need validation
The purple mouth keepout is a validation envelope, hidden in ordinary renders
Open frames reduce the thermal contact of H01; no cooling performance or C01 integration is provided
Sampled motion and camera segments do not prove complete robot swept clearance, full optical visibility or physical safety
